usual_baseline: Risk assessment on admission is usually done (93–100%) [1387][1685][2693]. The weak items are lying and standing BP, 25–34% [1596][1685][1880], and medication review after a fall, 9.09% [1794] and 22% [1742]. Call bell in reach 56% [1800]. Nationally, flat lifting equipment used in 22% [1169].
fix_that_works: Prompts built into routine. Education, SystmOne prompts and weekly MDT fall reviews: medication review 22% to 94% [1742]. Teaching, posters and aide-memoires: LSBP 32% to 83.3% [1596]. Huddle reminders and flyers: LSBP 34% to 68% [1685]. Stickers, teaching and handover reminders: call bell in reach 56% to 93.88% [1800]. Checklist and education: composite 65% to 90% [1880].
fix_that_fails: Continuous national audit moved slowly: flat lifting 22% to 29%, medical assessment within 30 minutes 52% to 60% [1169]. LSBP stayed at 65% after a checklist [1880]. LSBP was sometimes ticked as done when it was not [1685]. The call bell project showed no link with falls [1800].
consultant_advice: Lying and standing BP has been done often with the same result. More useful: audit medication review and deprescribing after a fall, which was 9.09% in one hospital [1794], or post-fall management such as CT head criteria [1171]. Measure falls or harm, not just process.
